title: Class 6 Science · Ch 1 Worksheet A · What is Science?
instructions: Answer all questions. Write neatly in the space provided in your notebook.

questions.question: Science is best described as
options: a way of understanding the world by observation and experiment
a list of facts to memorise
an old story passed from elders
a hobby unrelated to daily life
questions.answer: a way of understanding the world by observation and experiment
questions.explanation: Science is a systematic way of learning by observation and testing.

questions.question: _____ is the urge to ask questions about the world around us.
You can be a scientist by carefully observing things in your daily life.
questions.explanation: Anyone can practise scientific thinking; observing and questioning are the start.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why curiosity is important in science.
questions.answer: Curiosity makes a scientist notice unusual things and ask 'why' or 'how'. Without curiosity there are no questions to investigate, and so no science.
questions.explanation: Tests the link between curiosity and inquiry.

questions.question: Give one example of doing science in your daily life and explain why it counts as science.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Noticing that wet clothes dry faster on a windy day, asking why, and trying it on a still day to compare. It counts because it involves observing, asking a focused question, and testing.
questions.explanation: Tests applying the idea of science to daily life.

questions.question: Pick something you noticed today (e.g. why ice cubes float, why sound is louder near a wall). Write: (a) the observation, (b) a question, (c) a hypothesis, (d) one way to test it.
questions.answer: Sample: (a) Ice cubes float on water. (b) Why does ice float when most solids sink? (c) Hypothesis: Ice is less dense than water. (d) Test: weigh an empty measuring cup; fill with water at the brim; weigh again to find the mass of the water. Repeat with the same cup filled with crushed ice. Compare the masses.
questions.explanation: Open-ended; full credit for any thoughtful application of the four steps.
